articleTitle: A Small Target Detection Model Based on an Improved RT-DETR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Object detection, as one of the core tasks in computer vision, has been a focus of research in recent decades, thanks to the rapid development of deep learning technology. From R-CNN, YOLO, to SSD, RetinaNet, and DETR with Transformer, various algorithms have been developed at a rapid pace, including lightweight, end-to-end, 3D object detection, and small object, cross-modal detection, etc., which have achieved good detection results on various public datasets. However, the task of detecting small objects has not seen significant breakthroughs due to the fact that small objects occupy fewer pixels in images and often lack sufficient semantic features. In real-world scenarios, they are often subject to issues such as lighting, blurring, and obstacles, making it difficult to distinguish and detect them. The application areas of small object detection are very rich, especially on mobile devices, where balancing detection performance and model parameters is a challenging problem. In this paper, we adopt the RT-DETR model and replace the main branch's Basic Block with FasterNet Block to reduce the model's parameter count and computational cost, making it more suitable for deployment on mobile devices. We also fuse the output of P2 feature layer through the SPDConv module with the output of P3 feature layer to enhance the model's ability to extract features of small objects. The experimental results show that the improved model achieves good results on the Visdrone2019 drone dataset, especially in the performance of detecting small objects.

articleTitle: Research on Calibration Method of Joint Reduction Ratio for Industrial Robot Considering Dynamic Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The increasing application of industrial robots in advanced manufacturing demands higher pose and trajectory accuracy. Motion parameter identification and calibration are effective methods to enhance operational precision. This study addresses the angle error in industrial robot joints by introducing a novel joint reduction ratio calibration strategy that incorporates dynamic factors. The research primarily investigates the impact of rotational inertia and speed on error patterns. Experimental methods were employed to examine the distribution of joint angle errors in the first and second joints, which are significantly influenced by the robot's posture, under varying rotational inertias and joint speeds. Further analysis from the perspectives of servo follow-up error and reducer structure elucidates the variation mechanism of the reduction ratio under different conditions. A joint transmission error compensation method based on variable reduction ratio is integrated into the motion controller. Results indicate that the proposed calibration strategy reduces the rotational angle errors of joints 1 and 2 to less than 0.01° and 0.02°, respectively, under different rotational inertias and speeds. This approach significantly improves compensated joint transmission errors, providing robust technical support for enhancing the highprecision control of industrial robots.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Algorithms for High-dimensional Unbalanced Medical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: High-dimensional feature selection is a difficult issue in medical field, while the class imbalance problem existing in medical data can also seriously affect the classification performance of algorithms. To address the joint problem of high-dimensional feature selection and class imbalance, a new objective function and the SMOTE imbalance approach are performed on the Simple, Fast and Efficient (SFE) based high-dimensional feature selection algorithm, as well as incorporating the Metropolis criterion in the SFE algorithm to help the algorithm jump out of the local optimal solution. Finally, a feature selection algorithm based on high-dimensional unbalanced medical data (GOSFE) is proposed. Experiments are conducted on six public datasets, and the results show that compared with the SFE algorithm, GOSFE improves the G-means and Fl metrics by 6.75% and 2.53% on the SMK_CAN_187 dataset, and the G-means and Fl metrics by5.95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>and 3.42% on the Leukemia dataset, respectively. Meanwhile, the experiments show that the GOSFE algorithm can quickly search the subset of features with the highest classification accuracy, reduce the redundancy of high-dimensional data, and has a good potential for improving the high-dimensional imbalance problem of medical data.

articleTitle: Underactuated Ship Heading Control in Harbor Based on Model-Free Adaptive Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by restricted waters, uncertain model parameters, and strong environmental disturbances such as wind and currents during the harbor navigation of underactuated ships, this paper introduces a method for controlling ship heading using partial dynamic linearization, which operates without relying on any model information. Firstly, a partial dynamic linearization model is developed using the system's input-output data, and then the model is adjusted online with changing navigation conditions through pseudo-partial derivative estimation. Additionally, conventional model-free adaptive control methods applied directly to ship heading control in the body coordinate system can result in non-convergent control errors. To solve this problem, this paper introduces a model-free adaptive sliding mode control method. Finally, MATLAB simulation tests and a comparative analysis with the traditional model-free PID control method demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method and its strong robustness against environmental disturbances.

articleTitle: Assembly Sequence Planning Algorithm Based on Topological Ordering and its Simulation System Development
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Assembly sequence planning and its simulation are critical components in modern manufacturing. With the increase in the number of product components, the number of assembly sequences grows exponentially, presenting characteristics such as strong discreteness, large search spaces, and small feasible domains. The existing assembly sequence planning methods based on heuristic algorithms, such as particle swarms and genetic algorithms, are afflicted with shortcomings, including low solving efficiency and a proclivity to fall into local optimization during the solving process. To address these issues, this paper proposes a topology-ordered assembly sequence planning algorithm based on a greedy strategy. The algorithm employs a comprehensive evaluation index that considers both the part-level and the product-level in order to optimize the topological sorting process. It ensure that the output sequence are more compatible with the actual process. Additionally, a simulation system integrating interference checking, assembly sequence and path planning functions has been developed on the basis of the in-house Inte 3D software. The objective is to provide a set of intelligent assembly sequence planning tools for the manufacturing industry, with the aim of effectively shortening the product development cycle.

articleTitle: Underwater Pipeline Defect Detection Method Based on Active Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of marine exploration and the increase of submarine oil and gas transportation pipelines, the detection of underwater pipeline defects has become increasingly important. The existing defect detection technology has great advantages, but also has some limitations. Inspired by the active electrolocation system of weak electric fish, this paper proposes a new underwater pipeline defect detection technology based on frequency inflection points (FIP). In this method, the joint time-frequency spectrum (JTFS) is obtained by joint time-frequency analysis of the detection signal, and then the FIP corresponding to the characteristic defect is obtained by calculation and processing. The data show that there are obvious differences in FIP due to different materials and defect characteristics. In practical applications, the calculated FIP can be compared with the characteristic curve to obtain the defect information of the measured object. At the same time, this paper also carried out defect detection experiments on non-metallic objects. The experimental results show that the defect detection method proposed in this paper is convenient to use and has a wide range of applications. It has great potential in underwater pipeline defect detection and underwater robot applications.

Author Keywords: active electrolocation system of weakly electric fish

articleTitle: An Assist-as-Needed Controller with Fault-tolerant Region for Safe and Effective Training on End-effector Upper Limb Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an assist-as-needed position-based impedance controller for rehabilitation training of upper limb motor function impairments in patients. The controller establishes a fault-tolerant region around the movement training trajectory, allowing the upper limb to move freely in this space without assistance from the robot. For the movement out of the fault-tolerant region, the robot provides compliant assistance to guide the upper limb back toward the movement training trajectory. This approach minimizes assistance from rehabilitation robots and maximizes the patient's active participation, which could promote rehabilitation efficacy. This study not only simulates the robot arm but also established an equivalent model of the upper limb coupled with a robot model and implemented a human-robot interaction system for control simulation that enhanced the reliability and practicality of the rehabilitation training. The simulation results possess enhanced reliability and practicality, and to some extent, could validate the performance for safe and effective rehabilitation training.

articleTitle: Technology of Mobile Robot Localization Assisted byQRCodes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the improvement of productivity levels, people's demand for enhanced functionality and expanded application scenarios of mobile robots is increasing. Mobile robots are playing an increasingly critical role in several fields. Ensuring that mobile robots can achieve high-precision localization in various environments has become the basis for its role. However, traditional laser-based localization technologies suffer from significant errors in areas with indistinct environmental features. Firstly, the QR code is deeply studied, including its characteristics, classification and function principle in localization calculation. To address this, a method that utilizes QR codes for assisting in robot localization is proposed. To validate the proposed method, a specific QR code was selected and the key technologies for mobile robot localization were thoroughly studied. The method integrates QR code information using laser-based radar and the Cartographer SLAM algorithm to achieve accurate localization. To verify the research results, a Gazebo simulation platform for mobile robots was established, and the simulations and physical validations of the proposed method were completed. The results show that the QR code assisted localization technology can significantly improve the localization accuracy in the area with not obvious environmental characteristics. Moreover, through the research of mobile robot localization technologies, it has a significant promoting effect on the cultivation of students' engineering practice and innovation ability.

articleTitle: A Variable Stiffness Soft Gripper Based on Shape Memory Polymer and Giant Electrorheological Fluidic Layer Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In this study, we designed a soft gripper with variable stiffness based on shape memory polymer (SMP) and giant electrorheological fluid (GERF). The soft gripper integrates electrostatic layer jamming enhanced by GERF into a fast pneumatic network actuator. SMP is used to promote the stiffness performance of the gripper. We introduce the specific structure and important size of the gripper, and the fabrication process and method of the gripper has been displayed. The finger has a variety of variable stiffness modes, and different stiffness variation ranges can be reached by reasonably combining different modes. According to the designed soft gripper structure, we have made a soft gripper model machine, the bending experiment and variable stiffness experiment of the soft finger were conducted. Through experiments we found that the soft finger has good variable stiffness ability, its stiffness varies from 0.034 N/mm to 0.22 N/mm, is about 7 times. Moreover, the integration of SMP has a more positive effect on the soft gripper, which can still maintain the bending state after disconnecting the air pressure, the grasping more reliable. Finally, the prototype of the soft gripper is used to grasp objects, which can grasp things of different sizes, weights and shapes, and its effectiveness is verified. The gripper has good application potential in grasping fragile items.

articleTitle: Design of Helicopter Attitude Controller Based on Improved Explicit Model Following Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Attitude control was the key to helicopter flight control which was the internal loop of speed and trajectory control. So, design of the helicopter attitude controller was the focus in the article. Firstly, the explicit model and inverse model module in traditional explicit model control systems was discussed. Then, the feedback compensation module was improved by the closed-loop gain shaping algorithm (CGSA). Finally, compared to the traditional explicit model following control (EMFC) controller, the controller designed in this paper had a simpler and more efficient structure which was easy to implement in engineering and had promotional value.

articleTitle: Steel Surface Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In steel surface defect detection, the typical characteristics of defects are irregular shapes and relatively small proportions of corresponding structures, which pose a challenge for conventional detection models. To address the issue of low sensitivity to these structures, this paper proposes an improved algorithm based on YOLOv8 for steel surface defect detection. The core innovation of the proposed algorithm is the design of a novel C2f_DSC module, which incorporates dynamic snake-like convolution to replace part of the C2f structure, thereby enhancing the model's detection performance. The approach begins by applying a convolution operation to the input feature map, which extracts higher-level feature representations. The receptive field of the network is then increased by stacking Bottleneck_DSC modules, allowing the model to better capture context information. Additionally, skip connections are introduced, enriching the gradient flow and facilitating the extraction of multi-scale defect features with greater diversity. Extensive experiments conducted on the NEU-DET dataset—an open-source collection of steel surface defects provided by Northeastern University—demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results show a significant improvement in detection accuracy, with mAP50 and mAP(50-95) increasing to 81.6% and 47.0%, respectively. This demonstrates a substantial performance boost over the original YOLOv8 and outperforms other state-of-the-art detection models, making it a promising approach for real-world industrial applications.

articleTitle: Research on Wide Range Turbidity Detection Technology of Mine Water Based on Double Scattering Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulties such as wide turbidity range of mine water, poor measurement stability, explosion environment of coal mine and stable uploading, a kind of wide-range turbidity detection technology of mine water based on double scattering principle is proposed, and an intrinsically safe wide-range turbidity sensor for mine is developed. In terms of hardware, the sensor utilizes high-performance imported photodiodes and precision operational amplifier integrated circuits. On the software side, through meticulous optimization of the signal conditioning circuitry, adoption of advanced sampling, filtering, and bubble elimination techniques, as well as implementation of multi-stage linear compensation, the sensor's turbidity measurement range and accuracy are significantly enhanced. The sensor uses OLED display technology to realize low power consumption design. In the digital interface communication design, anti-interference design is adopted and EMC Lv.3 experiment is passed, which is very suitable for use in the environment of strong electromagnetic interference in coal mine. The experiment proves that the measuring range of the wide range turbidity sensor used in the mine can reach 0~5000NTU, and the accuracy can be controlled within 4% F. S. By integrating with the mine monitoring system, the stable real-time monitoring of mine water turbidity can be realized on the surface.

articleTitle: Multiple Multiplicative Neurons Model for Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In recent years, the single multiplicative neuron (SMN) model, rooted in polynomial design, has garnered substantial scholarly attention and practical application. Building on SMN research, this study introduces an innovative multiple multiplicative neurons (MMN) model designed to enhance model robustness and adaptability. The MMN model incorporates customized backpropagation (BP), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and a cooperative random learning particle swarm optimization (CRPSO) algorithm, offering significant advancements in optimization efficiency and performance. These augmentations are strategically devised to enhance the versatility and efficacy of the multiplicative neuron model within diverse applications. To empirically substantiate the proposed MMN model's effectiveness, two benchmark time series prediction tasks were undertaken. The ensuing results unequivocally underscore the superior predictive performance of the MMN model relative to both the SMN model and the conventional feed-forward neural network. While the BP algorithm was computationally less efficient and prone to local optima in non-differentiable scenarios, and the PSO algorithm exhibited sensitivity to initial values, the CRPSO algorithm overcame these challenges by maintaining population diversity and enhancing optimization through a cooperative stochastic learning mechanism. The evaluated algorithm (MMN-CRPSO) demonstrates a remarkable efficacy in error reduction within data measurements, achieving a precision level of one in ten thousand. This empirical demonstration not only substantiates the proficiency of the MMN model in time series prediction but also positions it as a promising advancement within the broader landscape of neural network modelling and time series analysis.

Author Keywords: cooperative random learning particle swarm optimization (CRPSO)

articleTitle: Research and Practice of CDN Accelerating Hot Internet Content Based on OLT
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: There are obvious differences between the popular network content accessed by end users covered by different OL T (Optical Line Terminal) network elements. The CDN (Content Delivery Network) network caches the popular content locally and schedules users to access it nearby through the DNS (Domain Name System) domain name system to achieve the content acceleration function. However, the traditional CDN cannot select different storage nodes according to the popularity differences of the content, and the user access scheduling can only be completed in the domain name dimension, unable to schedule different resources of the same domain name accessed by users to different node services. To solve the above problems, this paper innovatively proposes to reuse the idle board card position of the OL T device to set up a CDN logical sink node. Through the linkage of the hotspot identification algorithm and the BRAS information, it accurately judges the popular content accessed by users covered by different OL Ts, and caches the popular content to the CDN sink node. When users access, different nodes are selected according to the popularity difference of the content to provide services to users, so as to reduce the network transmission distance and improve the quality of service access for end users. Verified by the implementation in the existing network, this solution can significantly improve the hit rate and download rate of the service.

articleTitle: Lightweight Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Underwater robots frequently grapple with challenges such as false detection and missed detection due to factors like turbid water and low contrast of detected objects. These issues significantly hinder the efficiency and accuracy of underwater exploration tasks. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel lightweight underwater target detection method based on an improved version of the YOLOv7 model. The core innovation lies in the integration of the GhostNet network as the backbone of the proposed method. By leveraging GhostNet's efficient architecture, we manage to drastically reduce the overall parameter quantity and eliminate excessive redundant feature information within the network. This not only results in a more compact network model but also enhances the overall detection accuracy. Furthermore, to broaden the network's receptive field and capture more intricate details, we introduce the MP-D module. This module cleverly employs dilated convolutions to replace the conventional downsampling convolutions, thereby enabling the extraction of more precise positional information of small targets without incurring additional computational overhead. The experimental results underscore the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm. Compared to the original YOLOv7 algorithm, our method achieves a significant reduction in model size by 24.6MB and a notable decrease in parameter quantity by 35.3%. Moreover, it boosts the recall rate by 5.5% and the mean Average Precision by 1.2%, demonstrating its robustness and superiority in underwater target detection tasks.

articleTitle: Mixed Node and Edge GraphSAGE Based Schema Encoding for Text-to-SQL
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In text-to-SQL tasks, it is important to construct a model that is applicable in databases of different domains, and how to improve the generalization and induction capabilities of the model is a pivot challenge to be addressed. Traditional approaches are limited by the following shortcomings: 1) limited to transductive models, which do not perform as well as inductive models when generating embeddings for unseen nodes of graphs in cross-domain scenarios; 2) insufficient attention to the importance of structural information in relational databases and do not distinguish local and non-local relations. Therefore, we propose a Mixed Node and Edge Graph SAmple and aggreGatE text-to-SQL model, MNEGraphSAGE for short, which is based on graph sampling and propagation algorithm for node and edge features and converges faster. We give full attention to graph network edge features by mixing the iterative process of edge features and node features in parallel. We also adopt different aggregation methods for edge features of different distances. In the Spider dataset covering multiple domains, our method achieves 64.02% without the help of pre-trained models, outperforming other models of the same size.

articleTitle: Application of Untiree GO 1 in ORB-SLAM3 Map Building
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the increasing urbanization, the proliferation of highways has significantly increased the workload involved in highway maintenance. In particular, the maintenance inspection of tunnels plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and functionality of these vital transportation infrastructures. Robots for intelligent highway tunnel maintenance inspections present a promising solution to alleviate the associated costs and efforts. This research focuses on utilizing the Unitree GOI robot dog, equipped with the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm, for efficient tunnel maintenance detection. This study outlines the process of setting up the GOI robot dog environment from the ground up and employing ROS2 to transmit video captured by the binocular fisheye camera mounted on the robot dog to a customer PC. Subsequently, the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm is executed on the customer PC for map building to overcome the the problem that GOI dog machine does not have enough computility. Through successful experimentation, this study demonstrates the feasibility of employing the GOI robot dog in conjunction with the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm to generate accurate maps of real tunnel environments. This study improves the reliability of the GOI dog operation and solves the problem of the bad result of map building due to insufficient computility and indistinct images.

articleTitle: Fusion Model Based Identification of Anomalous Intrusion Behaviour in Network Facilities of Distributed Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Distributed networks, due to their huge systems in the communication process, data management, information transmission, etc., are weak in detecting and defending against increasing types of network intrusions, and there is an urgent need to design a more intelligent anomalous intrusion situational awareness model to cope with brand new network attacks and to guarantee the normal operation of the system. In this paper, we design an anomalous intrusion situational awareness model based on machine learning algorithms for the architectural features and defence deficiencies of distributed network systems, which is developed by combining a gated recursive unit (GRU) and an improved support vector machine (CTSVM), and enhances the system's ability to determine the detection of abnormal network traffic independently. Compared with the traditional machine learning model, the model shows the best performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and other rating indexes by testing and comparing 38 subtypes of anomalous intrusions on the NSL-KDD dataset, which provides new technical support to improve the network security defence capability.

articleTitle: Design of PMSM Controller with Continuous Function Reaching Law and Integral Sliding Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: An innovative improved reaching law (IRL) is introduced to overcome the inherent limitations found in the traditional sliding mode control (TSMC) that is based on the exponential reaching law (ERL). The ERL has been found wanting in its inability to concurrently achieve rapid convergence to the sliding surface and a reduction in chattering. The IRL addresses these issues by integrating a continuous function with an integral sliding surface, merging the advantageous aspects of both exponential and power reaching laws. This new approach abandons the conventional switching function in favor of a hyperbolic tangent function to create a unique continuous function reaching law. Through rigorous theoretical analysis, it has been shown that the IRL not only accelerates the reaching speed from the initial state to the sliding surface but also maintains certain switching characteristics while drastically minimizing chattering. With the IRL as its cornerstone, an improved sliding mode controller (ISMC) is developed specifically for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). To guarantee stability, a comprehensive Lyapunov stability analysis is performed. Both simulation and experimental results validate the practicality and efficiency of the ISMC. When contrasted with the TSMC, the ISMC exhibits a quicker response time and more precise tracking of the required reference position sinusoidal signal, all while successfully reducing chattering to a significant degree.

articleTitle: Design and Trajectory Planning of a Underwater Delta Robot for Marine Harvest
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper proposes and designs a Delta robot for underwater grasping, which is a challenging task due to the harsh environment and unpredictable conditions in the ocean. To achieve successful underwater grasping, the basic structure design and kinematics analysis of the Delta robot were carried out. The working space of the robot was determined and drawn to ensure that it can reach the desired location for grasping. Moreover, two trajectory generation strategies were designed based on different seabed conditions: rough seabed and flat seabed. The door-shape strategy is suitable for rough seabed conditions, while the target-oriented radial strategy is ideal for flat seabed conditions. The design of the control system and the software system of the robot were introduced in detail to ensure that the robot can operate efficiently and effectively. The construction of the prototype was completed, which included assembling the mechanical components, installing the electrical components, and testing the system. Finally, a basic seafood capture test was carried out to evaluate the performance of the Delta robot. The robot was able to complete the goal of fast capture, demonstrating its potential for underwater grasping applications. Overall, this Delta robot is a promising solution for underwater grasping tasks, offering fast speed, high stability, and adaptability to different seabed conditions.

articleTitle: Personalized Federated Learning with Collaborative Aggregation Networks for Multi-Site Brain Disorder Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In multi-site brain disease diagnosis studies, traditional centralized training methods necessitate sharing medical data, posing significant privacy risks. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving solution by enabling global model training through aggregating locally trained models from multiple data centers without sharing raw data. However, current FL approaches rely on a server-based network topology, where central server failure disrupts training. Additionally, data heterogeneity across sites often slows convergence and reduces accuracy. To overcome these issues, we introduce a decentralized personalized federated learning collaborative aggregation network (pFedCAN). This framework has two core components: (1) separating local models into shared and personalized layers, and (2) forming a collaborative aggregation network via similarity detection in the shared layers. Specifically, each center trains its local model, then separates it into shared and personalized layers. The shared layer is exchanged with other centers, while the personalized layer remains local. Data centers analyze similarities in received shared layers to build a collaborative network, where shared layers from similar centers are aggregated to refine the model. This approach flexibly adapts to varying levels of data heterogeneity, enhancing model training efficiency. Validation on public datasets, ABIDE I and ADHD, shows that the proposed method outperforms current leading techniques.

articleTitle: Parkinson's Disease Recognition Using Hybrid CNN-Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder that affects the physical and mental health of millions of people. Thus, the early detection of PD is significantly essential for timely intervention. In this paper, we propose a simple yet influential deep learning framework, named a Hybrid CNN-Transformer, for the automatic recognition of PD patients using MRI scans. In particular, the model architecture integrates the merits of CNN with the Transformer for feature extraction in different feature dimensions. The Transformer in the model also captures the long-range dependences, which enables the model to handle both local and global statements effectively. Our proposed method is evaluated on the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) dataset. Based on experimental results, our model performs better with a test accuracy of 80.51 %, precision of 80.49%, recall of 79.89%, F1-score of 0.80, and AUC-ROC of 0.84 compared with traditional CNN models such as VGG16 and DenseNet121.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Video Surveillance Recognition and Warning Method for Tornadoes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: A method for tornado formation recognition and early warning was introduced based on video surveillance. The video surveillance image is preprocessed, and then the GMM model is used to extract the background image 5 minutes ago. The static scene is used as the background, and the moving object is extracted by background subtraction. The foreground and background in the image are extracted to separate the region of interest (tornado target) from the background area in the image. Then the moving image is binarized and the pixel statistics are performed. Since the tornado has a shape feature of being large at the top and small at the bottom, this feature can be used to perform template matching and identification on the moving object. Therefore, the foreground 0-value pixel statistics are performed row by row from top to bottom on the foreground image. If the number of pixels in the upper part of the foreground image is greater than 1.5 times the number of pixels in the lower part, it is determined to be a suspected tornado image. Finally, after the monitoring personnel make a judgment and confirmation, a tornado warning is issued to the people in the affected area to reduce the loss of life and property.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Active Disturbance Rejection Control Technology for Quadcopter UAV in Flying Manipulator Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: As the core content of the flight manipulator system to provide a stable platform for the operation of the manipulator and achieve accurate grasping, the attitude angle control must have strong anti-interference control ability. In order to improve the robustness of the aircraft, a fuzzy active disturbance rejection control strategy for the quadrotor in the flight manipulator system was proposed. Based on the fact that the traditional ADRC integrates fuzzy control logic into the design of the nonlinear error feedback control law, which reduces the difficulty of adjusting the parameters of the traditional ADRC, and the fal function is used in the design of the traditional ADRC extended state observer, when the deviation is large, the gain of the observer will increase sharply, resulting in the decrease of the anti-interference ability of the system. For the above problems, the faln function is used, when the error is large, this function limits the gain of the system, so as to enhance the immunity of the system. The attitude model of the quadcopter UAV was built in the MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment, and the simulation effect of the traditional PID attitude control was compared under the condition of interference. The simulation results show that the designed attitude controller has good anti-interference ability under the condition of external interference. According to the attribute information of the physical platform, a 1:1 virtual simulation model is built in Solidwork, which can be imported into the Gazebo virtual physical simulation platform to verify the control effect of the controller, providing a method for the virtual simulation of the flight manipulator. According to the attribute information of the physical platform, a 1:1 virtual simulation model is built in Solidwork, which can be imported into the Gazebo virtual physical simulation platform to verify the control effect of the controller, providing a method for the virtual simulation of the flight manipulator.

articleTitle: Laser Weld Defect Detection Based on Laser Vision and Region Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a laser vision-based approach for detecting defects in steel laser welding. The Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) algorithm is combined with region growing to effectively segment point cloud data. This segmentation process leverages both local region features and the interrelationships among neighbouring points. Initially, the BVH algorithm is utilized to group the point cloud data, identifying optimal seed point locations for subsequent analysis. Subsequently, the region growing algorithm is applied, with the establishment of specific growth criteria to determine point inclusion within their respective regions. These defined growth criteria serve as guidance for expanding the regions from the initially selected seed points. This expansion process culminates in the derivation of segmentation results and facilitates the identification of defects. Importantly, this process eliminates the need for pre-emptive defect type confirmation or the conversion of 3D data into 2D data, as typically practiced in conventional point cloud processing. This enhancement significantly enhances detection efficiency. Experimental results underscore the effectiveness of this approach in overcoming potential interferences such as light source noise, leading to successful defect segmentation. At the same time, compared with other typical methods, our method takes the shortest time. Consequently, this method holds potential for detecting welding defects within industrial settings.

articleTitle: CNN Structure Optimization Based on MI-EEG Channel Information Density
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to effectively extract Motor Imagery Electroencephalography (MI-EEG) features and optimize a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for classification accuracy improvement. In this paper, 10 subjects were enrolled to collect the data of the motor imagery experiment with left-hand and right-hand holding. After data pre-processing, the information density of MI-EEG signals was determined according to the Phase Locking Value (PLV), and 20 channels with high information density were retained. The EEG after channel screening was used as the input signal of CNN. And according to the characteristics of the input data, the CNN network structure and parameters were optimised. The results show that the average classification accuracy of MI-EEG signals of 10 subjects is improved from 86.29% to 90.46% by using the optimised CNN classifier, and the accuracy of the optimised CNN classifier is also improved compared with EEGNet. The results confirm the significant effectiveness of the proposed method on improving the classification accuracy of MI-EEG signals.

articleTitle: Modeling a Cross-Domain Distributed Personnel Records System Based on Zookeeper and Erasable Bloom Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of cross-domain file query and file transmission difficulties in the current file system, an improvement scheme of personnel file management system based on zookeeper and erasable Bloom filter is proposed. The multi-node distributed system is constructed through the node monitoring and data synchronisation mechanism of zookeeper, and each sub-system uses Bloom filters to improve the efficiency of archive query, achieve efficient collaborative query between multiple archive systems, and improve the performance and scalability of the system. For the dispersed independent and huge number of stock archives, it is proposed to achieve fast positioning of single-point system based on Bloom filter filtering. There are frequent file transfer operations in the archive system, and the traditional Bloom filter can no longer meet the demand. This paper analyses the structure and characteristics of the traditional Bloom filter, and on the basis of the traditional Bloom filter structure, adopts the idea of collision counting to realize the erasable Bloom filter. Compared with the traditional Bloom filter, this method solves the problem of undeletable elements that exists in the traditional Bloom filter and effectively reduces the storage overhead of the counting Bloom filter. Experimental results show that the model can effectively achieve cross-domain archive query and archive forwarding, and maintain good performance and stability when the archive data increases.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Image Fusion Algorithm Based on Generative Adversarial Networks with Residual Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Addressing the challenges of limited information and low detection accuracy of single-modality imaging in power equipment fault detection, a multimodal image fusion method (ResGAN) using generative adversarial network and residual connectivity is proposed in this paper. The algorithm consists of two modules, including a feature extraction module and a feature reconstruction module. Firstly, the feature extraction module uses a two-channel convolutional neural network with weight separation and introduces a residual connection block (Resblock). Then the fused image is obtained using the feature reconstruction network. Secondly, the fused image undergoes a continual integration of feature data of the original image through an adversarial interplay involving both the dual discriminators and the generator. In addition, the neural network is constrained using a hybrid loss function of content loss and adversarial loss to achieve multimodal image feature fusion. The experimental outcomes indicate that the fusion method surpasses the quality of other frequently utilized fusion algorithms and can consequently be applied for power equipment fault detection.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of the Digital Twin Platform for Loading Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a construction method of the digital twin platform for an artillery automatic loading system. Taking a real fully automatic loading system as the research object, a corresponding digital twin visualization platform is established. And through projectile loading tests, the application and accuracy verification of the established digital twin platform are carried out. Firstly, the concepts of automatic loading system and digital twin are elaborated, and the challenges of applying digital twin technology in the field of artillery are pointed out. Then, this paper describes the construction process of the digital twin platform. The platform construction process mainly includes four important steps: (1) obtaining training data for the surrogate model, (2) establishing a surrogate model, (3) real-time data acquisition and communication, (4) platform design and modeling. In this study, the training data for the surrogate model is mainly obtained through finite element analysis and real projectile loading tests. The RBF method is used to establish a surrogate model for real-time calculation of the structural mechanical properties in the actual loading process. A sensor network composed of laser sensors, rotary encoders, and fiber Bragg grating sensors is set up to collect data. The TCP communication protocol is established for data transmission between the actual loading system and the digital twin platform. Finally, the functions of the platform are verified. The platform can realize the interaction between virtual and real data, monitor the mechanical properties of the loading system in real time, and the error of the surrogate model is not greater than 15%.

articleTitle: A Study on Redis-Based Aided Caching Pattern for Relational Database Hotspot Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low hotspot data prediction accuracy, complex prediction model structure, and non-uniform data caching structure of existing caching technology, this paper proposes a lightweight relational database hotspot data caching model, which realizes the relational database hot table data migration storage to the Redis caching database by constructing the hotspot prediction model and the data migration storage model (including KV-TO, KV-PA, and KV-FC), solving the I/O read/write bottleneck problem of relational database and reducing the interaction frequency with disk. Compared with the traditional hotspot prediction scheme, the hot table prediction model in this paper adopts the idea of cache elimination algorithm, simplifies the data model, and improves the cache hit rate by 17.67% and 10.19% compared with the traditional log monitoring model and hotspot data prediction model, respectively. Meanwhile, all three data migration storage models can achieve fast migration of hotspot data to Redis, in which the migration time of the KV-TO model is shorter; the memory utilisation of the KV-FC model is higher. Engineering practice shows that the model not only has low cost and fast efficiency, but also improves the throughput capacity of the database in high concurrency scenarios and achieves efficient access to massive hotspot data.

articleTitle: Formation Planning with Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) formation plays a pivotal role in diverse civil and military applications. In civil use, it can revolutionize tasks like precision agriculture, mapping vast landscapes, and enhancing emergency response. In the military, coordinated UAV formations are essential for strategic surveillance and tactical operations. Currently, much of the UAV formation research has been restricted to obstacle-free scenarios. However, the evolving landscape of modern missions demands UAVs to proficiently handle complex terrains. To overcome the hurdles of formation flight in such complex settings, scholars have proposed an array of methods. Control-based ones emphasize maintaining UAV stability and coordination, while trajectory optimization-based methods seek optimal flight paths. Our novel formation planning method combines multi-agent trajectory prediction and optimization. By integrating prediction outcomes into the optimization objective function, it achieves the dual goals of obstacle avoidance and formation integrity. Compared to prior techniques, our method stands out. It bolsters formation maintenance, ensuring UAVs stay in sync even amidst disruptions. Moreover, it streamlines the optimization process, saving computational time and resources. With this inventive approach, UAV formation flights in complex, obstacle-ridden environments will be more dependable and efficient. It paves the way for enhanced mission success rates and broader application possibilities, opening new vistas for UAV technology utilization.

articleTitle: A Dual-Direction Convolution Mixed-Attention Network for Facial Expression Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Facial expression recognition has remained a focal point due to its vital applications, such as medical diagnosis and human-computer interaction. However, the complexity of human emotion leads to a wide diversity of external expressions. Small inter-class differences and large intra-class differences are also significant challenges for effectively identifying facial expressions. In this paper, we establish a Dual-Direction Convolution Mixed-Attention Network (DDC-MAN) to enhance the recognition effect of CNNs. The DDC-MAN framework consists of a CNN backbone, a dual-direction convolution (DDC) module, a mixed-attention dual-direction feature fusion (MADDFF) module, and a multi-head spatial-channel attention (MHSCA) module. Specifically, our model first employs ResNet18 as the backbone for extracting facial features. The DDC module is then incorporated to capture facial texture information from two directions more effectively. Additionally, the MADDFF module is proposed to find key areas from both single and mixed attention across width and height directions. Finally, the MHSCA module is introduced to perform spatial and channel attention based on these key areas. Experimental results demonstrate that our DDC-MAN approach yields impressive improvements over state-of-the-art methods on the AffectNet and RAF-DB datasets.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Wake Measurement in Sea Based on Hyperspectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Based on the UAV and hyperspectral measurement technology, the spectral energy density of the wake center region and the kelvin region is obtained. In contrast, the spectral absorption peak of the two regions is little different. The kelvin wake can be regarded as the modulation effect of the target on the rough sea surface waveform, which does not change the spectral absorption coefficient of the sea surface itself, and the modulation degree of the wake in different regions is different. As a result, the reflection degree of the sea surface to the background light is different, so the wake region presents the characteristics of light and dark changes, the principle of which is consistent with the detection principle of the convergence and divergence of the sea surface in SAR.

articleTitle: Optimization Algorithm of Multi-Attribute Group Decision-Making Based on Information Entropy Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The problems of complex mathematical models, high computational complexity, and repeated parameter adjustments in the subjective and objective weighting method is studied. Such problems are generally defined as multi-attribute group decision-making models. Multi-attribute group decision-making models have been widely applied in fields such as achievement evaluation, scientific research performance assessment, and project review, and are a popular research direction in the field of artificial intelligence. How to balance the subjectivity among experts and the objectivity of attribute weights is a challenging problem in the research of multi-attribute group decision-making models. The entropy weighting method is firstly used to obtain the objective weights of attributes. Then, the grey correlation degree method is applied to adjust the subjective weight. Finally, based on the minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence method criterion reflecting the distance between different weights, an optimization model is established to solve the integrated weight. It is provided a feasible weight integration method based on information entropy theory for multi-attribute group decision-making. A numerical experiment shows the feasibility and practicability of the method. It is provided a new solution to the problems of prioritizing quantity over quality in the performance evaluation of scientific research in universities and research institutions, which can effectively promote the enthusiasm of scientific and technological workers for scientific research innovation.

articleTitle: Multi-Path Restorative Pre-Training with Localized Adaptive Graph Convolution for 2D Tooth Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Segmenting teeth in 2D oral CT images is crucial for diagnosing dental conditions. However, many current models for 2D tooth segmentation depend solely on end-to-end segmentation loss during training, which can fail to capture the image's intrinsic features. Additionally, neighboring regions may interfere with tooth segmentation, leading to less-than-optimal results. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Multi-Path Restorative Pre-training with Localized Adaptive Graph Convolution (MPRP-LAGC) for 2D tooth segmentation. The MPRP utilizes two paths—one for image reconstruction and another for tooth edge reconstruction — as auxiliary tasks for pretraining the segmentation model. This enables the model to better capture both global image characteristics and the specific features of tooth edges. After dividing the feature maps to correspond to the tooth, maxillary, and mandibular regions, dynamic convolution is applied to emphasize the distinctions between the tooth area and surrounding tissues in the feature space. Experiments on one publicly available 2D oral CT dataset show that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art models and accurately segments the boundaries of teeth, particularly where they meet the maxilla and mandible.

articleTitle: Orbital Analysis of Passive Dynamic Walker with Dual Arms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Unlike traditional models that predominantly consider lower limb dynamics, this research introduces the study of the passive biped walking with dual arms. The system's dynamic movement is represented through an optimization formulation, subject to constraints that ensure periodicity and optimal behavior. With optimization, the passive walker could generate natural biped locomotion with dual arm swing motion. Next, the study extensively investigates the effects of the arm's dynamic parameters on the overall locomotion, stability, and energy demand of the entire system. The results clearly demonstrate the impact of these dynamic parameters on stability, energy consumption, and step characteristics of the biped locomotion. Moreover, the insights gained from this study provide valuable guidance for the future development of robotic systems that more closely mimic human locomotion.

articleTitle: A Channel-Augmented Multi-Domain Graph Convolutional Network for Fatigue Driving Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a crucial cornerstone within the realm of brain-computer interface (BCI) applications, with its significance notably pronounced in the field of fatigue detection. However, the inherent limitations of EEG acquisition equipment during real driving scenarios have contributed to the constrained robustness of existing models. Moreover, most of recent methods failed to extract robust multi-domain features, leading to a suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel channel-augmented multi-domain graph convolutional network (CA-MDGCNet). Specifically, the initial EEG signals are enriched by incorporating supplementary virtual EEG channels, distinguished as learnable parameters within the network architecture. Then, differential entropy features are extracted from the augmented EEG signals. Following this, a multi-domain graph convolutional network is designed to encode high-level EEG features by means of convolutions in diverse paths, which is beneficial to integrating the characteristics extracted from multiple domains. Finally, the classification block derives the detection outcome from the refined feature maps. To substantiate the potency of the proposed method, the validation was conducted on the publicly accessible SEED-VIG. The proposed CA-MDGCNet not only demonstrates more promising performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches but also underscores the potential viability of our method for the realm of fatigue driving detection.

articleTitle: A Study on Capacity Expansion Plans for Hub Stations Based on AHP and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the launch of the new national Land-Sea New Corridor construction plan, expanding and upgrading hub stations has become strategically important for enhancing transportation efficiency, optimizing logistics costs, and promoting regional economic development. This study centers on Nanning South Station, a pivotal hub on this corridor. We developed an innovative evaluation model by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation to systematically assess the multifaceted benefits of hub station expansion. Unlike traditional models, our approach introduces a comprehensive evaluation index system tailored to the complex requirements of hub expansions, integrating economic, social, and environmental factors. Key indicators such as transportation efficiency, return on investment, and environmental sustainability were prioritized, with additional sub-indicators refined through expert input to capture a nuanced assessment. The model's practical applicability was validated through a case study at Nanning South Station, where it not only provided optimization suggestions but also demonstrated adaptability for broader use in future corridor expansions. This novel approach offers quantitative support for informed decision-making in the Land-Sea New Corridor's infrastructure planning.

articleTitle: Research on D3QN-PER Path Planning Method Based on LSTM-GRU Composite Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Reinforcement learning plays a pivotal role in Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) path planning by enabling the AUV to learn optimal navigation strategies through trial and error. However, traditional Deep Q Network (DQN) suffers from slow convergence and instability when applied to AUV path planning. In this paper, a Prioritized Experience Replay Dueling Double Deep Q-learning method based on the Long Short- Term Memory-Gate Recurrent Unit composite model (LSTM-GRU-D3QN-PER) is proposed to address this issue. Firstly, the Deep Double Q Network (D3QN) is used to mitigate the overestimation problem in traditional Q-learning algorithms and to improve the estimation accuracy of the value function, thus improving the stability and convergence of training. Secondly, the prioritized experience replay mechanism is employed in the method to enhance the sample efficiency of training and improve the convergence speed and stability of the algorithm. Finally, the Long Short- Term Memory-Gate Recurrent Unit (LSTM-GRU) composite model is employed to handle state information, resulting in the improvement of memory and cognitive abilities to obtain more favorable environmental information. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, experiment is executed on the Open AI Gym testing platform and validated in the Maze environment. Experiment results show that the algorithm with potential to improve convergence speed, stability, and learning performance.

articleTitle: Amplitude Identification for Ultrasonic Transducer Based on Instantaneous Current
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In industrial applications, the amplitude of piezoelectric ceramic transducers directly affects the quality and reliability of production. The vibration amplitude of the ultrasonic transducer is related to its own impedance of frequency-dependent. To maximize vibration amplitude and energy transfer efficiency, it is necessary to control the frequency of the ultrasonic transducer. However, the amplitude is difficult to obtain in actual industry. To address this issue, an electromechanical coupling model of the ultrasonic transducer is introduced, and it is proven in the BVD equivalent model that the amplitude is proportional to the amplitude of the dynamic branch current. A new ultrasonic transducer amplitude identification is proposed based on this model. Firstly, the driving voltage and current of the transducer are obtained. By utilizing the static capacitance characteristics, the instantaneous value of the dynamic branch current is derived. The extracted instantaneous current is proven to be directly proportional to the vibration amplitude, which successfully identifies the vibration amplitude of the transducer.

articleTitle: A Vision-Only Drone Formation Waypoint Navigation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have found widespread applications in various fields and scenarios, prompting extensive research on their formation control and route planning. However, in extreme application scenarios such as complex electromagnetic battlefields, existing studies often rely on radio frequency communication for data exchange between UAVs or utilize external sensors like GPS for positioning, which are susceptible to interference. To address this, we propose a method for distributed formation control of UAVs that solely relies on visual and inertial data, without data exchange between UAVs or the use of external positioning sensors like GPS. Drawing inspiration from the flight formations of migratory birds, our approach employs cameras to detect the orientations of neighboring UAVs. A simulation environment is constructed using a game engine to train a YOLO object detection network for reliable detection of other UAVs. Sub-sequently, utilizing geometric relationships, the positions of UAVs in the formation coordinate system are calculated, and our proposed formation control algorithm is applied to adjust the UAVs to their desired formation positions. Moreover, we employ the SIFT object detection algorithm to match images from the downward-facing camera of the UAV to satellite maps for obtaining global coordinates. Our introduced randomized navigator election algorithm selects a leading UAV for guiding the formation with higher accuracy along the intended route. Through simulation experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves comparable accuracy to traditional methods in most scenarios, while exhibiting strong robustness.

articleTitle: Deformation Analysis of Soft Pneu-Net Actuators in Free Space with Different Chamber Spacing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Soft pneumatic actuators (SPAs) are increasingly popular due to their easy manufacturing, simple actuation, and natural flexibility. However, there is currently no comprehensive model to predict how SPAs deform in free space when the spacing between chambers varies. In this paper, we develop a bending model based on the contact mechanics of the expanding membrane and the principle of virtual work. This model accounts for chamber expansion both with and without contact and includes the influence on gravity. To validate our model, we fabricated two types of SPAs with different chamber spacings and conducted experiments and simulations. Our results demonstrate that the model's predictions align closely with experimental data, the theoretical and experimental error less than 10% within 20 kPa, accurately forecasting the deformation behavior of SPAs.

articleTitle: Path Tracking Method of Forklift AGV Based on Fuzzy Adaptive PID
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Precise path tracking is essential for forklift AGVs (Automated Guided Vehicles) to safely and efficiently complete loading and unloading tasks. External environmental changes can significantly affect the path tracking accuracy of forklift AGVs, posing challenges to their operational reliability. To address this issue, this study began with a comprehensive kinematic analysis and pose error analysis of the forklift AGV, aiming to understand the underlying mechanisms that influence its movement precision under varying conditions. Based on these analyses, the research adopted the concept of hierarchical control to design both a traditional PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller and a more advanced fuzzy adaptive PID controller. These controllers were specifically tailored to adjust for lateral deviation and heading angle deviation, which are critical parameters in maintaining accurate path tracking. The effectiveness of the two controllers was rigorously tested through simulations and real-world experiments using MATLAB. The results from these tests not only validated the feasibility of both the PID and fuzzy adaptive PID controllers for path tracking but also highlighted the superior performance of the fuzzy adaptive PID controller. This advanced controller demonstrated a notable improvement in the linear path tracking accuracy of the forklift AGV, as well as enhanced operational stability, especially when faced with unexpected environmental changes. The findings suggest that the fuzzy adaptive PID controller, grounded in hierarchical control principles, offers a robust solution for improving the overall performance and reliability of forklift AGV systems.

articleTitle: A Course Recommendation Algorithm Based on Global Directed Graphs and User Behavioral Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Existing course recommendation methods typically rely on static course learning records to infer users' overall learning preferences. However, such approaches fail to account for the dynamic evolution of user preferences and short-term interests over time. In this paper, we propose a novel recommendation algorithm, referred to as DPGD, that incorporates a global directed graph and user behavior sequences to address these limitations. The algorithm begins by constructing a global directed graph based on user behavior sequences. This graph is then stored in a graph database to facilitate efficient access and analysis. This representation enables the model to capture both long-term learning preferences and short-term, evolving interests. Subsequently, we compute the similarity between behavior sequences using an appropriate similarity measure, which allows us to assign varying weights to relevant courses, ensuring that the recommendations reflect users' current learning needs. Additionally, we propose a global preference propagation strategy that accounts for the evolution of user preferences over time, thereby improving the accuracy and relevance of recommendations. The final personalized course recommendations are generated by calculating the ratings of the recommended courses based on the propagated preferences. Experimental evaluations on a real-world course learning platform dataset demonstrate that the proposed DPGD algorithm outperforms existing recommendation methods in terms of both effectiveness and feasibility, offering a promising approach for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Servo system Cascade Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on Motor Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The electromechanical servo system is usually implemented by three closed loops, with the inner loop being the current loop, the middle loop being the speed loop, and the outer loop being the position loop. The traditional system tuning method is the PI parameter trial and error method, which cannot achieve the optimal performance of the system. This article innovatively adopts the LADRC three closed-loop cascade control method. Compared with previous control methods, the control method applied in this article can ensure that the current loop, speed loop, and position loop control circuits all meet the requirements of the Bode theorem, which provides a basis for the control objectives. This article provides a detailed description of the selection methods for the control order, observer bandwidth, controller bandwidth, and loop gain of each control loop. This method was validated and ultimately achieved stable control of the electromechanical servo system.

articleTitle: Research on a Multi-Sensor-Based Wearable System for Monitoring Infant Vital Signs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In contemporary society, people lead increasingly hectic lives, and for families where both parents are employed, caring for an infant presents significant challenges. Maintaining constant vigilance over an infant's well-being during the night can be particularly distressing. Some disadvantages are associated with manual nursing, such as the high cost and the inability to achieve continuous monitoring at night. To solve this issue, the microchip STM32F103 was employed as the central control unit to develop a wearable intelligent monitoring system for tracking infants’ vital signs during sleep. A wearable design is employed by the system to monitor not only the baby's vital signs but also the baby's sleeping position. These data are wirelessly transmitted to a mobile phone, allowing parents to conveniently monitor their infant's vital signs in real-time. Moreover, in the event of any abnormal conditions, the mobile phone promptly emits a vibrating alert, preventing parents from missing the critical ‘Golden Hour’ for infant rescue, even during deep sleep. Through the analysis and processing of physiological signal data test results, it has been proven that accuracy and reliability are possessed by the equipment detection system. When the preset threshold is exceeded, the phone activates an alarm, successfully achieving the intended outcome through the implementation of the intelligent infant monitoring function.

articleTitle: Real-time Visual Perception for Rapid Grasping of Underwater Delta Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Underwater autonomous grasping of seafood is a very meaningful field in robot research. However, the grasping efficiency of existing underwater grasping robots is very low. In this paper, a Delta robot for underwater capture is built, and a visual perception framework suitable for the rapid grasping of the manipulator is proposed. Firstly, we use YOLOv5 to initially locate the target, and then use the stereo camera to obtain the depth and calculate the spatial coordinates. Secondly, we established a refraction model for the waterproof housing, based on the problem that the target may be occluded, it is proposed to install a camera on the moving platform of the Delta manipulator to solve the occlusion problem. The vision system transmits the spatial coordinates of the target to the inverse kinematics controller. Finally, the Delta manipulator is built in the air and this framework is applied to the manipulator to implement rapid grasping. Experiments verify the applicability of the proposed method. The moving platform of the robot successfully reached the target position within 1.5 seconds.

articleTitle: AntFuzz: Follow Ants to Find Food in Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Fuzzer is widely employed for vulnerability discovery and security assessment of software systems. Based on existing protocol fuzzers, this paper proposes a more efficient fuzzing solution called AntFuzz. It draws inspiration from ant colony algorithms, where ants use pheromones to find food. Similarly, seeds in AntFuzz require pheromones to guide their search direction. This work introduces a seed-centric multi-factor selection strategy. Specifically, the protocol state and code coverage assist in exploring a wider code space, while the coverage of predecessor basic blocks of vulnerability blocks helps trigger vulnerabilities more rapidly. By considering the low-frequency paths, states, and vulnerability blocks that seeds reach, seeds are given different probabilities of execution and mutation. Additionally, the network sockets of the target program are modified to Unix domain sockets to increase the throughput of fuzzing. The performance of AntFuzz is validated on real-world network service programs. Preliminary evaluation results indicate that compared to AFLNET, AntFuzz achieves up to a 50x increase in throughput, an 89% increase in code coverage, and significantly earlier triggering of vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: A Multi-scale Residual Network Based on the Multi-head Attention Mechanism for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have led to increased application in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for decoding motor imagery electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Nevertheless, current methods still present considerable challenges in effectively decoding these signals. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), most used in this domain, are constrained by limitations associated with their kernel size and inherently limited receptive fields. This restricts their capacity to fully capture the global spatial and temporal dependencies present in EEG signals, which is crucial for accurate decoding. In response to these limitations, we propose a novel approach: a multi-scale residual network based on the multi-head attention mechanism. This model is designed to overcome the constraints of traditional CNNs by incorporating a multi-head attention layer, four convolutional layers, and a pooling layer, which enable the extraction of global and local features. To verify the effectiveness of our model, we conducted an experiment involving left- and right-hand fist imagery. We evaluate the performance of our model against several state-of-the-art models currently used in the field. The experimental results indicate that our model performs significantly better than the baseline model, with superior decoding accuracy, and our model is faster and more stable in the convergence of the loss function. It achieves an optimal balance between model complexity and accuracy, which makes it more advantageous in practical applications.

articleTitle: NLOS Error Suppression Method for UWB Indoor Positioning based on TDOA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: As people's requirements for indoor positioning accuracy continue to increase, indoor wireless positioning technology has developed rapidly. Among the many wireless positioning technologies, ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless positioning has quickly become a hot topic in today's indoor positioning research due to its strong anti-multipath interference ability, low power consumption, and high positioning accuracy. However, due to the complex and changeable indoor environment, UWB devices are interfered with by various factors in this environment, resulting in the inevitable NLOS (non-line-of-sight) error in the wireless positioning system, which hugely affects the positioning accuracy of the positioning system. For the problem of NLOS propagation in indoor pedestrian positioning due to received signal strength indication (RSSI), this paper proposes a locating algorithm that predicts RSSI using a motion model and corrects NLOS measurements. Firstly, the pedestrian's position and RSSI are predicted using a motion model, and NLOS errors are detected and corrected. Then, the pedestrian's activity range is estimated using step length prediction, and an improved trilateration algorithm is used for positioning. Finally, the Fang-unscented Kalman filter is applied to optimize the positioning results and obtain an optimized estimation of the position. Simulation experiments indicate that this method can validly improve locating accuracy, suppress large NLOS errors, and is an effective positioning method in NLOS environments.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Subspace Identification for MIMO LPV System with Minimum Euclidean Distance of State Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The rigid-flexible coupled variable mechanical system, as a typical multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system, poses significant challenges in system modeling, control design, theoretical analysis, and practical engineering implementation due to its complex dynamic characteristics and the interactions among multiple variables.
