To address these challenges, this paper proposes a subspace closed-loop identification method for MIMO linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems based on the minimum Euclidean distance of the state sequence. First, through the subspace closed-loop identification algorithm, a non-unique form of the linear time-invariant state-space (L TI-SS) model with the minimum Euclidean distance state sequence is obtained. Then, using the least squares method, a similarity transformation matrix is computed to convert the non-unique form of the LTI-SS model into the standard model. Finally, the global linear parameter-varying state-space (LPV -SS) model is obtained through cubic spline interpolation. The proposed method is experimentally validated on a single-degree-of-freedom ball screw test rig and simulated on a two-degree-of-freedom motion system. Through simulation and experimentation, the calibration determination coefficient of the LPV MIMO model is above 0.98, demonstrating the superior accuracy of the model. Compared with traditional modal standard models and controllable standard models, the proposed method requires fewer data to achieve the specified model accuracy, improves the computational efficiency of the identification process, and reduces experimental and data collection costs. This provides an effective solution for modeling rigid-flexible coupled variable mechanical systems.

articleTitle: CrCo- Mlgcn: A Cross-scale Co-learning Based Multi-Level Graph Convolutional Network for Brain-Computer Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) decoding is a crucial foundation for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology. However, existing methods commonly concentrate on time-frequency features and overlook positional information, thereby failing to fully utilize the high spatial resolution advantages of fNIRS. Furthermore, some methods employ multi-branch structures, but they fail to consider the cooperative interaction between the branches, leading to suboptimal performance. To address these limitations, we propose a cross-scale co-learning based multilevel graph convolutional network (CrCo-MLGCN). Specifically, a multi-level graph convolution module is crafted with three branches to extract features from different levels, including local, regional, and global levels. Then, a cross-scale co-learning module is employed to harmonize the model's multiple branches, ensuring efficient parameter utilization and preventing redundancy. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed CrCo-MLGCN outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, confirming the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Development and Application of SCM System Based on the IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: To realize the online monitoring and collection system of soil composition information, this paper proposes a multi-parameter online monitoring and collection system for soil composition. First, the soil composition parameters are collected by intelligent multi-parameter sensors to realize low-cost on-site monitoring at a high temporal and spatial scale; then, the data monitoring and collection unit and the data cloud display platform are designed, and finally, the soil composition monitoring (SCM) service system that can monitor data in real-time is constructed. On this basis, a soil comprehensive index quality evaluation model is established to evaluate and predict the quality of the soil. Through experiments on the whole system, the results show that the SCM system proposed in this paper performs well in the reliability and real-time performance of data uploading and monitoring, and can be widely applied to the field of SCM in various environments.

articleTitle: A Dual-Graph Learning Framework with Sparse Adaptive Embedding for EEG Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: EEG brain networks capture the complex relationships between multiple brain regions, providing rich information for emotion recognition. However, most existing methods rely on dynamically random initialized adjacent matrix, which limits their ability to effectively model emotional features across different brain regions. Additionally, these methods typically ignore the importance of synchronously modeling both adjacent and long-distance channels, resulting to suboptimal emotion recognition performance. In this paper, we propose a novel dual-graph learning framework with sparse adaptive embedding (DGLF-SAE) for EEG-brain-network emotion recognition, which includes a global hypergraph sparse adaptive embedding (GHG-SAE) module and a local adjacency graph sparse adaptive embedding (LAG-SAE) module. Specifically, the GHG-SAE module is designed to capture global relationships by associating long-distance channels, while the LAG-SAE module focuses on learning local relationships by modeling adjacent channels. We validate the effectiveness of our proposed DGLF-SAE on the SEED and SEED-IV datasets, with experimental results (98.05% and 92.83% on SEED and SEED-IV datasets, respectively) demonstrating that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process Based Health Evaluation of Business Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the development of business application systems of large enterprises to cloud and system architecture to micro services, the system scale and the complexity of call interaction and business coverage are increasing, and the improvement of system complexity brings new challenges to the evaluation of system operation status. O&M personnel need to regularly evaluate the health status of the systems to identify risks and hidden dangers in system operation in a timely mode. The health degree evaluation of information systems that performs comprehensive analysis and assessment of the system to determine whether the operational status and capabilities meet expectations, is a typical multi-objective and multi-level problem. To provide a feasible solution of this problem, this paper proposes a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) based health evaluation method. Specifically, a multi-layer indicator system for business system health evaluation is constructed by combining it with the experience of operation and maintenance (O&M) experts. Moreover, an FHAP-based weight calculation method is proposed to obtain the weights of the indicators. The FHAP-based method can reduce the impact of O&M experts' subjective evaluation on the overall health score. Furthermore, a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) based health evaluation method is proposed. An empirical analysis is provided to make the proposed method more accurate. This method can simultaneously complete the scoring of system health and the positioning of hidden dangers in the business system.

articleTitle: Recognition of Loosening Position of Reactor Windings Based on FBG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The shunt reactor plays a crucial role as a reactive power compensation device, and its operational condition directly affects the safety and stability of the power grid. Among the various mechanical faults that can occur in reactors, loose winding is particularly significant. Currently, the identification of reactor winding looseness primarily relies on methods such as analyzing vibration signals and frequency response. However, these methods are limited by their susceptibility to environmental noise interference and relatively weak online diagnostic capabilities. Strain signal can provide a direct indication of the state of winding looseness; however, there is currently a dearth of research focused on analyzing the winding status using strain analysis. To tackle these challenges, this study takes a 10kV reactor as an experimental platform and gathers data from the winding with Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors. After processing the collected wavelength signals through cleaning and decoupling, this paper introduces a diagnostic method that incorporates an improved SVM based on the Black Hole Optimization algorithm and Principal Component Analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that by utilizing FBG signals and the diagnostic framework proposed in this study, the accuracy of identifying loose winding in the reactor is significantly enhanced. The study holds the promise of offering new insights into the identification of winding looseness.

articleTitle: Research on Testing Method for Broken Rail Monitoring Equipment Based on Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Broken rail monitoring equipment is essential for ensuring the safety of train operations, and it is necessary to conduct functional and performance testing before the equipment is put into operation. Considering the safety and order of line operations, laboratory testing methods are typically used, employing simulation boards to mimic actual rails. Since the rail is an inductive element, its impedance characteristics are closely related to the frequency of the electrical signal. Accurately simulating the impedance transmission characteristics of the rail under different scenarios and conditions is vital to implementing these testing. To achieve this, we utilize real measured data of rail impedance under different scenarios and frequencies, and establish an equivalent model of rail impedance characteristics using ensemble learning algorithms. This model takes the application conditions of the broken rail monitoring equipment as input and determines the impedance parameters of the signal during rail transmission. Based on this, a rail simulation board can be designed, and a track circuit and broken rail monitoring equipment testing platform can be set up, enabling scientific and efficient testing in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Swin Transformer Encoder and Local Attention Network Via Transfer Learning Strategy for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The effective segmentation of retinal blood vessels is an important means for diagnosis of fundus diseases. However, recent segmentation methods often ignore the global dependence of retinal blood vessels and have poor segmentation capability to small blood vessels. In addition, these methods are trained on limited datasets, resulting in a weak generalization ability. To solve these problems, we propose a new method based on Swin Transformer encoder and local attention network. First, Swin Transformer is used as an encoder to extract the global dependence of retinal blood vessels which can improve the continuity of blood vessels in segmentation results. Then, a local attention network based on edge detection module and coordinate attention module is developed to enhance the segmentation ability of the method to small blood vessels. Finally, a transfer learning strategy is also utilized in this paper. The encoder of our proposed method is pre-trained on ADE20K to enhance the generalization ability. Our proposed method is evaluated on three retinal image datasets: DRIVE, STARE and CHASE_DB1. The results demonstrate that the method proposed in this paper has better performance than others.

articleTitle: Joint Fault Diagnosis of a Hydraulic Hexapod Robot Based on 1D Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Leg joints are important motion actuators for hydraulic hexapod robots. Joint failures in a hexapod robot can directly lead to instability of the whole mechanical system, therefore, it is important to establish a fault diagnosis system to recognize joint faults instantly. In this paper, we propose a fault diagnosis method based on principal component analysis (PCA) and one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (lDCNN) for hexapod robot joint failures, named PCA-IDCNN. The original data is collected using angle encoders and displacement sensors. To improve the data quality and accuracy, the Kalman filter method is applied to fuse the data, reducing noise and enhancing the overall signal reliability. The Kalman fusion signal is input into PCA for compression, where it reduces the dimensionality of the signal while retaining important information. The compressed signal is passed through IDCNN, which utilizes filters to extract features from the signal. Finally, the classification process is performed using the extracted features to identify and categorize different classes within the signal. Experiments are conducted on a self-developed hydraulic hexapod robot. The results show that the proposed method can effectively identify hexapod robot joint faults, with an accuracy of 99%, which means that the PCA-IDCNN method is feasible in practical applications.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Trajectory Planning for Cooperative Source Seeking
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the cooperative source seeking problem via a networked multi-vehicle system, and proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-based trajectory planning scheme for the system. In contrast to most existing works, the source position of this work is determined by multiple types of signal fields, and each vehicle in the network is responsible to take measurements of a type of signal field. In another word, a single vehicle cannot localize the source position and must cooperate with its neighbors. To cooperatively localize and simultaneously reach the source position, the vehicle is equipped with a trajectory planning scheme that combines consensus algorithm for cooperative source seeking and an RL-based algorithm for maximizing the value of its corresponding signal field. Thus, each trajectory planner only requires measurements of a field and relative positions between neighboring vehicles, which is especially appealing to global position system (GPS)-denied environments. Simulations are provided to validate the efficacy of the proposed trajectory planning scheme. The RL-based trajectory planner actively leads the vehicle to positions with higher field measurements, without the need for gradient or absolute position information. And we demonstrate the successful deployment of the model learned in single vehicle settings to the cooperative source seeking task.

articleTitle: Shared-Specific Feature Enhancement and Dual Distilled Contextual Graph Refinement Network for Multimodal Conversational Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Emotion Recognition in conversation (ERC) is a crucial task in building empathetic machines. Previous studies usually treat multimodal (i.e., visual, audio, text) equally and rarely focus on the shared and specific features among different modalities, leading to the redundancy of multimodal features. Besides, the extraction of contextual information in a dialogue and multimodal knowledge transfer remains challenging, which results in the inadequacy of capturing relational and contextual semantics. To solve these issues, we propose a Shared-Specific Feature Enhancement and Dual Distilled Contextual Graph Refinement Network (S2FE-D2CGRN) for ERC task. Specifically, a shared-specific feature enhancement module (S2FEM) is first designed to enhance the text-guided shared semantics and make the specific features discriminative. Second, to refine and distill the contextual knowledge, a dual-distilled contextual graph refinement module (D2CGRM) is investigated, which includes a contextual graph construction and a two-stage knowledge distillation. Extensive experiments on two multimodal public datasets show the effectiveness of our proposed method compared with the state-of-the-art methods, indicating its potential application in conversational emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Bionic Ankle Joint Based on Tensile Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Combined with the morphological structure and tensile structure of the human ankle joint, a bionic structure of the ankle joint based on the tensile structure is proposed in this paper, in view of solving the problems of poor adaptability and poor structural flexibility of traditional bionic foot mobile robots in complex environments. Firstly, the bionic design method is used to analyze the mechanism design and configuration, by constructing the equivalent mapping model of the human ankle joint. Then, ANSYS software, Matlab numerical calculation and ADAMS are used to simulate and verify the theoretical numerical calculation results of spring deformation. The results show that the error of the experimental and simulation results is less than 3.7mm, and the designed ankle joint mechanism could realize the movement on a slope of 15 degrees. Furthermore, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed structure are verified, which extend the design method for the legged robot with adaptive walking ability.

articleTitle: The Comprehensive Evaluation Method for The Visibility Ability of ATCT Based on BP Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Airport Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) is one of the most important facilities at civil aviation airports. The location and height of ATCT will directly affect the controller's observation and judgment. In order to evaluate and compare the visibility capability of different tower construction schemes, a comprehensive evaluation method is set up. This method includes building an index system of obligatory and preference indicators, forming calculation methods for each indicator, and establishing a comprehensive evaluation model. In the evaluation model, two networks have been constructed based on Coefficient Strategy (CS) and Level Strategy (LS) respectively. Selecting a certain airport in East China as a case study, CS-BP and LS-BP network models of 5-10-1 in topology have been set up after 12000 typical samples for training respectively. The research results show that LS-BP network has the smaller Mean Squared Error (MSE) and greater regression coefficient compared to CS-BP network. And the results of CS-BP were similar to Traditional Strategy (TS). Therefore, selecting LS-BP network to evaluate calculated indicators of given schemes and considering that scheme 3 was best. The entire method can serve as a reference for decision-making by air traffic control unit.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale-Rhythm Attention Feature Contrastive Learning for Epileptic Seizure Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The electroencephalogram (EEG) signals based epileptic seizure prediction remains a pivotal technique to improve the living standards for epilepsy patients. However, recent prediction models focus on the local feature extraction with smaller receptive field, which ignores multi-level global feature changes in pre-ictal period. Besides, traditional supervised or semi-supervised learning strategies requires sufficient data in individual patient, and it is difficult to handle the representation learning of imbalanced samples of intra-patient EEG data, yielding a suboptimal performance in predicting seizures. To overcome above limitations, a multi-scale-rhythm attention feature contrastive learning (MSR-AFCL) model is proposed for the prediction of seizures in individual patients. First, a feature extractor called the multi-scale-rhythm (MSR) employs multi-scale dilated convolution module and multi-rhythm power spectrum density (PSD) estimate module, so as to extract multi-level spatio-temporal features and rhythmic temporal-spectral features with large receptive field. Then, an attention feature contrastive learning (AFCL) strategy is developed, and it has the capability to dynamically adjust the intra-class and inter-class distances of attention fusion representations. The experimental results indicate that our proposed MSR-AFCL model achieves outstanding seizure warning when evaluated on the publicly available CHB-MIT dataset, and it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Hybrid Electric Fish Optimization Algorithm: Integrating Stagnation Label and Levy Flight Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The Electric Fish Optimization Algorithm (EFO) is renowned for its robustness and global search prowess, yet it faces challenges like premature convergence and local optimum entrapment in complex, high-dimensional spaces. To tackle these issues, this study introduces an enhanced EFO, dubbed SLLF-EFO, which incorporates the Stagnation Label and Levy Flight strategies. By integrating advanced techniques like Good Point Set Theory and the Golden Sine Algorithm, SLLF-EFO boosts EFO's search capabilities. It employs a variable step size Levy flight to counteract passive electric field positioning stagnation problem and utilizes a stagnation label strategy to escape local optimum. Benchmark function-based experiments demonstrate SLLF-EFO's superior performance over EFO, offering faster search speeds and higher optimization accuracy in complex environments. This enhancement not only bolsters EFO's robustness and reliability but also holds significant implications for its future applications.

articleTitle: MIFF: A Unified Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification with Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Multimodal data, including spatial views and radar data, provide additional information that can enhance the accuracy of hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. While many studies have integrated multimodal data to boost performance, they often involve structurally complex models or are tailored to specific modalities, lacking a unified framework for HSI classification. To address this, we propose the Multimodal Information Fusion Framework (MIFF), a unified structure designed to simultaneously learn features from various modalities and integrate this information effectively. Our method consists of three key modules: feature extraction, filtering encoder, and unified decoder. The feature extraction module uses convolutional layers to extract features from different modalities and convert them into feature tokens. The filtering encoder applies interactive attention to enhance modality-specific information and facilitate cross-modal interaction and filtering. Finally, the unified decoder integrates the features from multiple modalities and produces the classification results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach effectively integrates multimodal information, significantly improving classification performance and validating the framework's feasibility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: An IoMT Based Epileptic Seizure Predictor Using Dual-Path Temporal-Spectral Encoded Spatial Dynamic Graph Convolution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent and uncontrolled seizures, severely impacting the safety of patients' lives. It is a challenging task to accurately predict seizures before its occurrence, and timely alarm patients to take appropriate measures to reduce the consequence of seizures. This work proposes an accurate and smart seizure warning predictor, named Seiz-Predictor, which is designed on the basis of the Internet of Medical Thing (IoMT) framework and constructed with a seizure prediction algorithm coupled with a mobile warning application. The Seiz-Predictor employs a dual-path temporal-spectral encoded spatial dynamic graph convolution network (DPTSE-SDGCNet) to enhance seizure prediction accuracy. Additionally, a compatible seizure warning mobile application is developed for seizure alarming, location recording, and interacting with cloud-based databases for further reference by doctors. The designed Seiz-Predictor offers several key benefits, including (1) We propose a novel lightweight network structure more suitable for epileptic seizure warning predictors, achieving more accurate predicting and shorter identification time in the public dataset. (2) A seizure warning mobile application is developed for cloud-based database connectivity, enabling computation of patient epileptic states for doctoral reference. Experimental results on the public CHB-MIT dataset demonstrate that the sensitivity of 96.1% and a false prediction rate of 0.086/h, outperforming the most recent investigations.

articleTitle: Chat, Summary and Diagnosis: A LLM - Enhanced Conversational Agent for Interactive Depression Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Depression is a significant mental illness that affects how individuals express their emotions and engage with others, making communication challenging. Most depression assessment tools utilize self-report questionnaires, such as the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). These psychometric instruments can be easily adapted to electronic forms. However, this approach cannot provide human-like explanations and interactions, leading to a poor interactivity. Furthermore, we have identified critical limitations in previous prompting methods. They are either constrained to queries using a single identifiable relation, or being agnostic to input contexts, making it difficult to capture variabilities that occur across different inference steps. To solve these issues, we develop a large language models LLM-enhanced conversational agent for depression detection, which makes it more effective and interactive. Specifically, we first explore an iterative knowledge-aware prompter (IKP), a new prompting paradigm which inject specific knowledge from language models progressively for multi-step reasoning, which learns to synthesize prompts conditioned on the current step's contexts. Second, our proposed system introduces a multi-step diagnosis (MSD) approach. Our system not only delivers a diagnosis but also generates a symptom summary through interactive conversations. Our proposed agent enables users to have interactive natural language dialogues with the system, enhancing their personalized comprehension of mental states. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the iterative knowledge-aware prompter design.

articleTitle: Real-time Object Detection Based on Mamba and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Amidst the swift progress in deep learning, the YOLO series has redefined the standards for real-time object detection. The incorporation of the Transformer architecture into YOLO models has significantly broadened their receptive fields and enhanced their feature extraction capabilities, thereby markedly improving detection performance. Nonetheless, this enhancement also leads to increased computational demands. To address this, our manuscript proposes an improved YOLOv8 object detection model that integrates a State Space Model (SSM) to overcome its previous constraints in accuracy and speed. Specifically, we've proposed the MambaCSP module and embedded it into the neck and decoupled modules. By employing depthwise separable convolutions and channel shuffle operations, we've tailored branches for both classification and regression tasks. These innovations not only bolster the model's feature extraction prowess but also maintain its computational efficiency. Our proposed method has demonstrated an average improvement of 1 % on the COCO dataset compared to the YOLOv8 model.

articleTitle: AB-LSTM: Long Short Term Memory with Artificial Bee Colony for Predicting Coal Mine Gas Concentration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The efficacy of gas concentration prediction is of utmost significance as it hinges on a well-defined theoretical foundation. Such a foundation is essential for bolstering preventive measures and facilitating the effective control of gas-related disasters within mining operations. The gas concentration prediction is carried out by integrating the improved Artificial Bee Colony algorithm, abbreviated as AB, with the long short term memory network (LSTM). Through the application of AB optimized LSTM, the prediction accuracy of LSTM is remarkably enhanced. The AB-LSTM gas concentration prediction model was established by meticulously selecting temperature, dust, and wind speed as the principal factors that have a profound impact on gas concentration and combining them with comprehensive laboratory test data. The outcomes obtained from this model vividly demonstrate its robust generalization capabilities. It is highly proficient in predicting both the evolving trends and peak values of gas concentration with remarkable precision. This proficiency not only powerfully underscores the model's reliability but also highlights its immense potential as a valuable and indispensable tool. It offers crucial theoretical insights and technical support that are vital for the comprehensive prevention and control of gas disasters in coal mines, thereby safeguarding the safety and well-being of miners and the overall stability of mining operations.

articleTitle: FedTMatch: Self-Supervised Federated Semi-Supervised Learning with Dynamic Threshold
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Federated semi-supervised learning (FSSL) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address the challenges of data privacy and the scarcity of labeled data. Most existing algorithms adapt the pseudo-labeling and consistency regularization methods in traditional semi-supervised learning (SSL) to exploit raw data from unlabeled clients. However, these methods always use the same high fixed threshold to filter out noisy pseudo-labels for each class, without considering the varying learning conditions and difficulty levels associated with different classes, resulting in a decline in the performance of global model, especially under non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) settings. To this end, we propose FedTMatch, a learning framework which adjusts the threshold for each class based on the learning status of each client. Furthermore, we introduce a self-supervised rotation loss in unlabeled clients to increase the utilization of raw data and correct the feature space formed by pseudo-label data to weaken the impact of Non-IID data distribution on global model's performance. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Process Machining Errors of Frame Parts Based on State Space
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The critical processing characteristics of components are key in ensuring product accuracy and quality consistency. This paper focuses on the key machining characteristics of frame parts and develops a multi-process machining error prediction model based on the state space theory to anticipate machining errors. Firstly, the error sources such as reference error, fixture error, and machine tool geometric error during the multi-process processing of frame parts are described using the homogeneous coordinate transformation theory, multi-body system theory, and error transformation theory. Secondly, a multi-dimensional model is constructed using the above error sources to predict the machining error process. Lastly, the sensitivity analysis of the multi-process machining error prediction model is performed using partial derivatives to study the contribution of each error source to the multi-process machining error prediction model during the processing of frame parts. The model's effectiveness is verified by taking the machining process of the external surface key machining feature of frame parts as an example, and the contribution of each error source to the errors of the key machining feature of frame parts is further explained.

articleTitle: INN: A Deep Correction Network for High-Dynamic Inertial Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Inertial navigation has gained extensive application because it solely relies on built-in Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) devices. Nevertheless, due to its inherent accumulative integral error, inertial navigation is often integrated with other external devices in practical situations, which unfortunately leads to unavoidable privacy breaches. To address these issues, an Inertial Navigation Neural Network (INN) is designed to generate high-precision position estimations without relying on any other auxiliary information. The INN model consists of attitude correction and velocity regression modules. The attitude module employs a convolutional network to correct the attitude information, and the obtained rotation matrices are then fed into a recurrent neural network to regress incremental velocities and produce high-precision positions. The proposed model is validated on the simulated trajectories based on the Precise Strapdown Inertial Navigation System (PSINS) toolbox. Experimental studies demonstrated that the proposed method has a significant corrective effect on high-dynamic strapdown inertial navigation settings. The accumulated position errors are an order of magnitude smaller than those of traditional track reckoning algorithms and achieved a comparable performance with integrated navigation.

articleTitle: Self-Data-Driven Modeling for Fault Diagnosis of RV Reducers in Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The health state of RV reducers plays a significant role in reliability and productivity of industrial robots. Due to the complicated structure and nonlinear dynamic behavior, it is difficult to construct a precise dynamic model of RV reducers. Aiming at the wear degradation monitoring of RV reducers, this paper develops a self-data-driven modeling method based on only proprioceptive sensor signals of robotic joints, including the torque, position and velocity. The baseline model of the ob-servation traj ectories is constructed by statistically analyzing the monitoring data under the healthy stage. A nonparametric modeling technique, i.e., functional principal component analy-sis (FPCA), is used to generate the principal components of the model automatically driven by the monitoring data. With the wear degradation of RV reducers, the observation trajectories will deviate far from the baseline model. Based on this phenom-enon, the real-time observation trajectories are reconstructed on the principal components. The trajectory reconstruction er-ror (TRE) signal is calculated to visualize the wear degradation of RV reducers. Through an experimental demonstration in a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) robot manipulator, it is found that the proposed method is more effective than commonly used momentum-based residual signals in the wear degradation mon-itoring of RV reducers.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Space Robotic Arm Based on Adaptive Non-singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of trajectory tracking for space robotic arms under the influence of system uncertainties and external disturbances. To tackle this problem, we propose a novel adaptive non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (ANFTSMC) strategy. This method extends the traditional non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) by integrating an adaptive reaching law, which enhances overall performance. This design allows the control rate to dynamically adjust according to changes in the system state, ensuring rapid convergence of both trajectory tracking and velocity errors to zero, despite uncertainties and disturbances. Furthermore, the proposed controller achieves shorter error convergence times compared to conventional NFTSMC. The stability and rapid convergence of the controller are validated through Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, numerical simulations confirm the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control
adaptive non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: A Control Algorithm for an Aerial Co-Manipulation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: During aerial co-manipulation, addressing the disturbances caused by the motion of the lower UAV on the aerial dexterous manipulation platform and the perturbations induced by the manipulation platform's own movement, as well as the issue of the inadequate number of existing simulation platforms, this study introduces an adaptive sliding mode control approach that leverages radial basis function neural networks and establishes a simulation platform for aerial comanipulation within the Gazebo environment. In the control method, the Lagrangian equation is employed for standardized modeling, and the model is simplified through projection. The universal approximation property of neural networks is utilized for adaptive rate optimization. Additionally, a sliding mode algorithm grounded on the exponential reaching law is implemented to bolster robustness. To further mitigate chattering, the hyperbolic tangent function is employed. Finally, the results were verified through trajectory tracking in Matlab/Simulink, ensuring that the system converged in about 1 second and achieved micron-level multi-channel tracking error accuracy, effectively reducing chatter. The Gazebo simulation platform sets up three aerial dexterous manipulation platforms capable of performing basic aerial tasks, and control stability is verified using PID algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on the Development Status and Future Trends of Foreign Unmanned Ground Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: In recent years, it has been observed that the army's intelligent and unmanned weapons and equipment have played a remarkable role in close combat during local wars, armed conflicts, and counter-terrorism operations. Furthermore, their utilization has evolved from individual soldiers and sporadic usage to cluster deployment. Combining with the operational situation, this paper divided the development of foreign unmanned ground equipment (UGE) into three stages (application exploring, gradual maturity and dominant battle), and analyzed the main characteristics of UGE's overall development (top-level design for traction, supporting construction for foundation and technology advantage for guidance). At the same time, the classification methods of foreign UGE were discussed in detail according to the classification of function (reconnaissance and surveillance equipment, fire strike equipment and comprehensive support equipment), and the development trends of foreign UGE were summarized as intelligent, modularization, swarm, flexibility, stealth and autonomy. The aim of this paper is to provide a theoretical reference for advancing the construction of the armyUGE.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Vision Transformer with Local-Global Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The extraction of multi-scale features from input images is crucial for computer vision tasks. However, some backbone networks based on visual transformers lack the ability to effectively extract multi-scale features or use relatively simplistic methods to do so. This paper proposes a novel multi-scale visual transformer, called Multi-Scale Extraction Transformer (MSET), designed to proficiently tackle a range of downstream visual tasks. MSET incorporates innovative concepts of Multi-Scale feature extraction Embedding (MS Embedding) and Local-Global self-attention (LGSA). MS Embedding uses a unique architecture convolutional layer method that constructs hierarchical residual-like connections, allowing for the extraction of multi-scale features at finer granularity levels. Meanwhile, LGSA integrates local and global dependencies within the self-attention module, reducing computational complexity while facilitating connections between the global and local features of the image. The importance of position information in the embeddings and the impact of amplitude on model performance are also considered, allowing MSET to handle position bias information of variable size in the input image and to ensure stability during training. Numerous experiments have demonstrated the significant advantages of MSET over most existing state-of-the-art backbone networks across various visual tasks, including image classification, object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Algorithm Based on Multi-Dimensional Community Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The traditional collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm only focus on the behavioral data between users and items, and ignore the impact of the features for users and items on the recommendation effect. Therefore, with the increasing number of users and items, data sparsity and cold start have gradually become challenges. Aiming at the problems of data sparsity and cold start of the collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm, this paper proposes a collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm based on multi-dimensional community detection, called multi-community collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm (MCCF). This paper introduces user features and item features to the traditional association network of users and items. Considering the construction of the association network among user features, users, items and item features, the Louvain algorithm is used for community detection from three dimensions of user features, user ratings and item features. The similarity between user preferences is calculated by Jaccard algorithm. Finally, the recommendations from multiple communities are combined and Top - K recommendation is made based on the final list of recommendations. Comparison experiments with the traditional collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm on MovieLens dataset show that the average precision of MCCF is improved by 8.3%, which can effectively alleviate the data sparsity and cold start problems.

articleTitle: Acquiring Quadruped Motion Styles Through CPG and Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Quadrupedal robots often display a rhythmic and cyclical pattern of movement. Central pattern generators (CPG), which can generate rhythmic signals, are extensively used to control biomimetic robots because of their resemblance to the locomotion mechanisms of actual vertebrates. Nevertheless, achieving stable walking in the desired direction can be challenging when solely relying on CPG signals to control joints for quadruped robots. This study suggests combining CPG and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) as a means to achieve stable locomotion in quadrupedal robots. By setting various parameters of the CPG, we generate a library containing various joint trajectories. Through DRL, we optimize the locomotion capabilities of quadruped robot for diverse motion styles generated by different set of CPG parameters. The experimental results in the simulation indicate that our method can maintain a steady forward motion on flat ground while executing a wide variety of motion styles, and it also possesses good exploratory capabilities in unstructured environments.

articleTitle: Transformer Text Recognition Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: As an important equipment in the power system, the text information on transformer nameplates mainly relies on manual collection, which is inefficient. Therefore, it is necessary to find a high-precision method to automatically identify the text information on transformer nameplates. However, there are many problems with the current scene text recognition algorithms in transformer text recognition, such as recognition errors caused by text blur and diverse backgrounds, as well as recognition omissions caused by paint coverage. This article provides a deep neural network FCRNN with fully connected encoding layers that can automatically recognize text within transformer image text boxes. Our network is extracted by the MV3 (Mobilenet V3) network, encoded by the FC network, and finally processed by the RNN network to obtain recognized text content. The text recognition network in this article achieved better recognition results than peer recognition networks on a self-made transformer pruning dataset. The text recognition results of transformer images through transformer text detection network and transformer text recognition network were also introduced, indicating the feasibility of transformer nameplate text detection and recognition. The FCRNN proposed in this article has better recognition accuracy for self-made transformer text recognition datasets while ensuring network performance. A lightweight network architecture can make the network easy to quantify and deploy on mobile devices.

articleTitle: Temporal-Spectral Multi-Scale Sub-Band Common Spatial Pattern Algorithm for Motor Imagery Brain-computer Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Motor Imagery Brain-Computer interfaces (MI-BCI), as one of the most common paradigms, has widespread applications. However, the leading common spatial pattern encoding algorithms can be prone to over-fitting and sensitive to noise. This study aims at extracting accurate temporal and spectral information which is related to the motor imagery. To address these challenges, we propose a novel multi-scale sub-band mixed temporal-spectral common spatial pattern (msSBMCSP) algorithm. This method improves the adaptability of MI-BCI to inter-subject or inter-session variabilities. The framework involves several key steps: preprocessing raw EEG signals followed by segmentation into epochs using a sliding window technique. Each epoch is further divided into multiple sub-bands at various scales. Depending on the frequency scale, two distinct CSP spatial filtering methods are employed. This results in sub-block CSP patterns for each frequency band, generating a multi-scale CSP feature set with time and frequency overlaps. These features are then compiled into a comprehensive global feature dictionary. A sparse regression technique is utilized to score these features based on their discriminative power, allowing for the selection of the most informative features and sub-blocks to construct a sparse subset. Ultimately, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) is trained on this refined feature set to accurately decode motor imagery tasks. The new algorithm was verified on two public datasets and achieved state-of-the-art performance. The dedicated handcrafted features are computationally cheap and easy to be deployed in practical BCI applications.

articleTitle: Control Algorithm of Two-Wheeled Mobile Robot Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: For the complex multi-input multi-output two-wheeled mobile robot(TWR) modeled, after the dynamics analysis found that there is a coupling between the state variables. When decoupling control using PID, although it can achieve a high degree of accuracy, there is still a more obvious coupling phenomenon between the state variables. Aiming at the problem of strong coupling of state variables and loss of control effect, it is proposed to design a controller for the TWR system using an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) algorithm, which can reduce the coupling degree by the extended state observer (ESO), so as to improve the control performance of the robot. Firstly, a reasonably simplified TWR dynamics model is analyzed, and a reasonable controller is designed and proved to be stable. Then, based on ADAMS View and MATLAB/Simulink, a TWR control simulation model is built, balance, steering and self-stabilization control experiments are simulated. Simulation results of the ADRC control are compared with those using PID. The results show that the balance control of the ADRC improves the RMSE by 87.4% and significantly improves the coupling state. Besides, ADRC has a smaller range of fluctuation during system oscillations, which significantly improves the performance of the TWR with high robustness.

articleTitle: DS-SGAN: Driving Style-Guided Spatial-Graph Attention Network for Trajectory Prediction of Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Vehicle trajectory prediction is a crucial and challenging task, especially in complex traffic scenarios involving multiple vehicle interactions, due to the complexity of the road environment and the variety of driving styles exhibited by different drivers. Prediction models ignoring influences of surrounding vehicles/roads and driving styles may produce unrealistic results and have low prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper introduces a novel driving style-guided trajectory prediction method based on a generative adversarial network. The generator utilizes LSTM and graph neural networks to encode relevant information about the target vehicle and the surrounding scene. To enhance the model's predictive capabilities further, it introduces a spatial-graph attention mechanism, which can pay attention to more important information in the spatial domain, to capture influences of surrounding vehicles/roads and generate reasonable predicted trajectories. We introduce unsupervised clustering to distinguish different driving styles and use discriminator to ensure that the generator generates trajectories conforming to the corresponding driving styles. Therefore, the entire framework is capable of not only generating accurate predictions but also aligning with the potential driving behaviors exhibited by drivers. To validate the efficacy of the proposed method, extensive evaluations are conducted on the Argoverse motion forecasting benchmark. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms other competitive approaches.

articleTitle: Improved Integral Nonlinear Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Aerial Dexterous Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The aerial dexterous manipulation system, as a combination of unmanned aerial vehicle technology and robotic arm technology (UAM), shows great potential in the execution of complex tasks. This study focuses on the coupling problem encountered by the system in aerial operation and proposes a novel control strategy based on improved integral nonlinear active disturbance rejection control (SNLADRCI) technology. This strategy establishes a rigid body model of the quadrotor aircraft through the Newton-Euler method and takes the robotic arm as the influence of the external disturbance source, which simplifies the model construction and is more suitable for industrial applications. By simplifying the traditional nonlinear function, not only the observation ability of the observer is improved, but also the difficulty of parameter adjustment is simplified. In addition, this study incorporates a nonlinear integral term to optimize the handling of static errors with a view to improving the overall performance of the system. By constructing an airborne dexterous operating system platform based on SNLADRCI, this study conducted experimental tests using MATLAB/Simulink and Gazebo simulation environments, and the test results effectively verified the reliability of the control method and its excellence in performance.

articleTitle: Path Tracking for Intelligent Vehicle Considering Steering Delay Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: As a crucial process in autonomous driving systems, path tracking control determines the safety and ride comfort of intelligent vehicles. However, the response delay of the steering actuator is commonly not considered in control tracking algorithms. The steering delay may directly impact the control accuracy, particularly when the target path curvature changed rapidly. This may lead to lower control precision and system oscillations, resulting in vehicle instability. Therefore, this paper proposed a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control algorithm considering steering delay characteristic that can avoid such problems. Firstly, the response delay characteristics of steering actuator is modelled as first order delay model and the model parameter is identified. Secondly, the actuator model is integrated into the vehicle model, and the optimization objective function of the discrete LQR in the infinite time domain is constructed. Then the optimal control feedback can be solved from the Riccati equation. Next, by designing the control feedforward item, the steady lateral error can be eliminated, and realizing the path tracking control considering steering delay characteristic. Finally, in the simulation environment, the control accuracy of the proposed steering delay LQR method, is compared with the original LQR and MPC algorithm under various test conditions to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Defense Framework for Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning Based on Client-Server Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL), various defense schemes are examined, resulting in the proposal of a comprehensive strategy that incorporates both client-side and server-side measures. This defense strategy is based on Dropout and LOF (Local Outlier Factor) outlier detection techniques. The model's resilience against data poisoning is enhanced by applying the Dropout technique on the client side. At the same time, the LOF outlier detection algorithm is utilized on the server side to identify potential abnormal model updates. Experimental results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, demonstrating a significant reduction in the Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 88.11% to 1.62% on the FMNIST dataset, and from 95.45% to only 0.25% on the EMNIST dataset. The success rate of backdoor attacks is notably diminished, confirming the strategy's strong backdoor defense capabilities.

articleTitle: Body Partition Refinement Dynamic Graph Convolutional Network for Skeleton-based Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) are the most commonly used methods recently and have greatly pro-moted research on skeleton-based action recognition. Aggregating features guided by a topology graph and generating adja-cency matrices with semantic edges in the topology graph are important for the task. However, building a simple and applica-ble graph is a challenging problem. In this work, we construct a novel body partition refinement dynamic graph convolutional network (BPR-DGCN) for skeleton-based action recognition, in which we propose a new body partition refinement dynamic graph convolutional module (BPR-DGCM) to efficiently extract representative features. Furthermore, by combining the traditional physical connection graph with our proposed body partition connection graph, we construct a body partition refinement dynamic graph convolutional unit (BPR-DGCU), which adopts a channel grouping strategy to learn a shared dynamic topology graph as a generic prior for all groups and refine it with chan-nel-specific body partition connection graph for different groups. Our BPR-DGCN outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the NTU RGB+D 60 dataset.

articleTitle: Temporal-Spectral Generative Adversarial Network based Multi-Level Consistency Learning for Epileptic Seizure Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Recently, deep learning techniques have been extensively explored and offer an efficient means for predicting epileptic seizures. However, due to the variability between different domains in the features of electroencephalogram (EEG) data, most of the existing methods only use the limited training data of the target subject, which is difficult to fully cover the data distribution and thus degrades the model performance. To solve this problem, a novel temporal-spectral generative adversarial network based multi-level consistency learning (TSGCN-MLCL) strategy is introduced in this paper. Specifically, the multi-level consistency learning (MLCL) strategy optimizes the seizure prediction model by training from three levels, i.e., inter-domain, intra-domain and inter-sample, which realizes the data distribution alignment of the source and target domain from multiple views. Second, considering the problem of limited labeled data in the target domain, we introduce the temporal-spectral generative adversarial network (TSGCN) to augment new training data, which generates high-quality simulated EEG samples according to the temporal-spectral distribution of real signals, and improves the finetuning process on the target domain. Our proposed approach attains a sensitivity of 96.7%, accompanied by a false prediction rate of 0.072 per hour, as demonstrated on the publicly available CHB-MIT epileptic seizure dataset. This performance surpasses that of current state-of-the-art studies, affirming the effectiveness of our methodology.

articleTitle: MAAS-Net: Efficient Multi-Scale Attention Aggregation Supervision Network for Tire Tread Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Overlap detection plays a critical role in ensuring tire safety performance, as defects like overlapping anomalies due to mold aging and wear elevate the risk of tire blowouts. However, traditional edge detection algorithms entail a cumbersome manual parameter adjustment process and are limited to fixed hardware equipment scenarios, thereby compromising the flexibility and robustness of surface defect detection. Moreover, conventional image segmentation methods often fall short in achieving high-precision segmentation of the tread area. In this paper, we introduce MAAS-Net, a network employing a U-shaped encoder-decoder architecture. Integrated within are Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) after each decoding stage to generate multi-resolution attention feature maps. These maps are progressively fused into Multi-scale Aggregated Supervision (MAS) to enhance the model's capacity to discern features across various levels and scales. Additionally, to enhance the model's accuracy near the tread edge area, we propose a post-processing method named ContourFix. Leveraging data augmentation and multi-task learning, ContourFix aims to replace unstable prediction values near the edges with high-confidence prediction values inside the target area. The efficacy of these techniques is evaluated using a dataset of 3D tire tread. Experimental results demonstrate that MAAS-Net significantly outperforms conventional semantic segmentation models in segmenting tire treads, and ContourFix effectively enhances the accuracy of the segmentation model near the regional boundary.

articleTitle: Empathy in Robotics: Empowering Emotional Connections in Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: Through a comprehensive review of literature and empirical studies, the study aims to analyze the importance of empathy in HRI, identify key components of empathetic interactions, and propose strategies for enhancing empathetic capabilities in robots. The paper will now include a detailed description of the experimental setup used to evaluate the emotion recognition model, specifying architecture, training parameters, and performance metrics. Incorporating empathetic features in robots leads to more engaging interactions, fostering trust, social bonding, and cooperation. The findings underscore the necessity of concrete ethical frameworks and solutions to address challenges associated with empathetic AI systems.

articleTitle: Trust Mechanisms in Decentralized Federated Learning: Enhancing Model Parameter Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: With the increasing demand for data privacy protection and the enhanced computational capabilities of edge devices, decentralized federated learning (DFL) has emerged as a key paradigm for distributed training. Unlike traditional centralized federated learning, DFL enables peer-to-peer communication for exchanging model parameters without relying on a central server. However, the presence of heterogeneous (non-IID) data often leads to performance degradation due to discrepancies in data distribution across different clients. Moreover, effectively controlling the progress and quality of model aggregation across nodes poses a significant challenge in DFL. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework, called Decentralized Federated Learning with Adaptive Trust and Consensus (DFL-ATC). This framework leverages a trust mechanism that assigns dynamic weights to the contributions of neighboring models by evaluating the feature outputs between clients. Additionally, we design an exponential scheduler to adjust the consensus step size, achieving a balance between model aggregation and handling data heterogeneity. Extensive simulations demonstrate that DFL-ATC achieves significant accuracy improvements compared to commonly used federated learning algorithms such as FedAvg and decentralized algorithms like D-PSGD.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Tracking Algorithm Based on Task Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The active tracking technology of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has significant applications in fields such as military operations, environmental monitoring, disaster response and traffic management. However, two major challenges greatly affect the performance of UAV active tracking in practical scenarios: (1) The presence of uncertain obstacles in the environment, which may cause issues such as occlusion and collisions, severely affects the UAV's tracking ability. (2) The randomness of target behavior can result in degraded tracking algorithm performance or even tracking failures. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel deep reinforcement learning algorithm based on task decomposition, which integrates the advantages of traditional heuristic methods and machine learning approaches. Firstly, a parallel neural module network is designed to decompose the UAV active tracking task into two sub-tasks: obstacle avoidance and target tracking. This task decomposition effectively reduces the complexity of the problem. Secondly, a two-stage curriculum learning framework is introduced, where the policy network of the agent is gradually trained by adjusting random obstacles to enhance training efficiency and algorithm performance. Finally, multiple simulation environments with random targets and obstacles are constructed to validate the stability and robustness of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating that it can effectively achieve tracking and obstacle avoidance in unknown environments.

articleTitle: YOLO-CD: YOLOv5-Based Neural Network for Empty Position Recognition of Dispatch Center
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Industrial Automation, Robotics and Control Engineering (IARCE)
abstract: The mine dispatch room plays a critical role in ensuring workplace safety by enabling security personnel to monitor and respond swiftly to emergencies. Detecting whether the dispatch room is unoccupied is essential to maintain continuous monitoring and prevent potential safety risks. This study addresses the challenge of automated vacancy detection in dispatch rooms, which is complicated by unique environmental characteristics and the issue of imbalanced sample categories. To overcome these challenges, we utilized screenshots extracted from a mine's safety analysis and warning system as experimental data. An improved YOLOv5 model was proposed, integrating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance its ability to focus on critical features of the human body while reducing the influence of background noise. Furthermore, a decoupling strategy was applied to mitigate recognition errors caused by low-sample categories, improving model robustness in detecting rare but critical scenarios. Experimental results validate the enhanced performance of the proposed model, showcasing its capability to accurately identify whether the dispatch room is vacant in real-world conditions. By enabling real-time monitoring and alerting, this research contributes to the automation of safety protocols in mining operations, reducing the reliance on manual supervision and improving overall safety management efficiency. This methodology offers a scalable solution for intelligent safety monitoring systems across similar industrial settings.
